headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared document/data handling creates prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways; no direct evidence of stronger isolation or locking.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests documents, data, and workflows, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can run browsers. If PaddleOCR output is fed into Cognee or shared files, attacker-controlled document content could be treated as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is copied into Cognee inputs or a shared workspace
IF either agent parses document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OCR output into Cognee
Add a manual review step before any document-derived prompt is executed
Restrict shared folders to read-only for one agent
Tag OCR outputs as untrusted metadata
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between OCR and memory ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch documents, and Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data. PaddleOCR processes documents/images and has network egress allowlisted, so sensitive content could flow through both systems if they share files or pipelines. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF the same documents contain personal or finance data and are processed by both agents
IF either agent uploads file contents to a remote backend during normal operation
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of shared workspaces
Process only redacted copies through PaddleOCR
Confirm both agents use separate service accounts
Review outbound destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory, and PaddleOCR can run browsers. Both also have allowlisted network egress, so they can contend over shared files, APIs, or browser state if orchestrated together. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so overlapping writes or state races are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or API-backed resource
IF browser state or session memory is shared across runs
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer per shared resource
Use per-agent browser profiles
Serialize jobs through a queue
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can transform documents into extracted text, and Cognee stores decisions, workflows, and schema structures. That creates a pathway where OCR errors or hallucinated structure become authoritative memory if Cognee consumes PaddleOCR output without verification. The pair lacks documented validation steps, so the cascade is credible in default pipelines.
conditions: IF Cognee ingests OCR output as trusted input
IF downstream workflows act on extracted text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of OCR extractions before ingestion
Store confidence scores alongside extracted fields
Reject low-confidence OCR segments
Compare against source documents for critical fields
requires-engineering: add validation gates before workflow execution

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee touches personal data and finance data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If regulated documents are routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge, especially because both profiles show only docs-only evidence and no explicit compliance controls. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance documents are processed by both agents
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two processing steps
mitigations: Classify regulated documents before processing
Block unsupported data classes from OCR pipelines
Set a shared retention policy for intermediate artifacts
Log data-flow destinations for audits
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement
